features.description: New module `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/notify_discord.py` mirroring the public shape of `notify.py`. Functions: `is_available() -> bool` (True iff webhook URL resolves, passes URL shape validation, and disable env not set), `notify(event: NotifyEvent) -> bool` (posts to webhook, returns True on 2xx, False on any failure incl. URL missing / malformed / network error / non-2xx response). Webhook URL resolution order: (1) `JARVIS_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` env, (2) `~/.jarvis/discord.json` with key `webhook_url`, (3) None → returns False. URL shape validation runs BEFORE any network call (urllib.parse.urlparse → require scheme in {http, https}, non-empty netloc, no whitespace); malformed URLs return False without invoking urlopen, so tests can assert zero outbound network attempts. Honors `JARVIS_NOTIFY_DISABLE=1` (same env as notify.py — single off-switch silences ALL sinks). Honors `JARVIS_DISCORD_DISABLE=1` for sink-specific silencing. Uses `urllib.request` (stdlib only — no `requests` dependency; matches smoke_test_storage.py precedent). Network call has a hard 5s timeout. Never raises; all failure modes return False and log a single stderr warn-once-per-process line so operators see it without spam. Payload v1: `{username: 'Jarvis', content: <markdown body>, allowed_mentions: {parse: []}}` — `allowed_mentions.parse` is ALWAYS empty in v1 (no @mention rendering even if event.body contains `<@USER_ID>` or `@here` literals). Per D003, v1 generates no @mention CONTENT either; the body strings in F003 emit sites contain plain prose. Future mention support (operator-configured user IDs to ping on escalation, via `~/.jarvis/discord.json`'s `mention_user_ids` array) is recorded as deferred (D003). Discord webhook URL secret discipline: file is gitignored (`~/.jarvis/` is outside repo), URL never appears in committed code or test fixtures (tests use `https://example.invalid/webhook` placeholder, RFC 2606 reserved TLD).

(2) `notify_discord.notify(event)` returns True on 2xx, False on every other path; never raises. (3) URL resolution order is env → json → None, with env winning when both present. (4) Malformed URL (missing scheme, missing netloc, non-http(s) scheme, contains whitespace) returns False WITHOUT invoking `urllib.request.urlopen` — tests assert urlopen was called zero times. (5) JARVIS_NOTIFY_DISABLE=1 silences this sink (parity with notify.py). (6) JARVIS_DISCORD_DISABLE=1 silences this sink without affecting notify.py. (7) Network calls have a 5s timeout; timeouts return False without raising. (8) Failure modes emit one stderr warn-once-per-process line, not per-event spam. features.description: Compact internal event envelope shared by both sinks AND adaptation of the existing notify.py terminal sink to consume it. New module `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/notify_event.py` defining `NotifyEvent` (frozen dataclass) and `dispatch_event(event)` (fans the event to all configured sinks honoring level matrix). Envelope fields: `kind: str` (extensible vocabulary, common values: volley_start, volley_terminal, gate_paused, gate_cleared, breaker_tripped, signoff, calibration_required, unit_mismatch, config_required, quota_warn), `severity: str` ('info' | 'action_required' | 'escalation' — closed vocabulary), `plan_id: str`, `feature_id: str | None`, `body: str` (markdown, sink-agnostic; both sinks render directly), `action_link: str | None` (file path / file:// URL — REQUIRED when severity=='escalation', enforced at dispatch_event entry), `timestamp: datetime`. Level matrix: PLAN_BOUNDARY_KINDS = {'volley_start', 'volley_terminal', 'signoff'} (closed set, defined as module constant; future kinds added explicitly via list edit, not implicitly). quiet → severity=='escalation' only. normal (default) → severity in {'action_required','escalation'} OR kind in PLAN_BOUNDARY_KINDS. verbose → every event. `JARVIS_NOTIFY_LEVEL` env reads quiet|normal|verbose; unknown values fall back to normal with stderr warn-once. dispatch_event calls notify.notify and notify_discord.notify in sequence, never raises, returns `{'terminal': bool, 'discord': bool}`. Terminal-sink adaptation: notify.py's existing `notify(title, message, *, subtitle=None, group=...)` keyword-arg signature stays as the public terminal-render primitive. New shim function `notify.notify_event(event)` projects NotifyEvent onto title/subtitle/message/group: title=`Jarvis [{plan_id}]`, subtitle=`{kind}` (e.g. 'breaker_tripped'), message=`body[:140]` (truncated to fit notification UX), group=`plan_id` so a per-plan notification stack can be batch-cleared. dispatch_event calls notify.notify_event (NOT the legacy notify directly) so call-site behavior is centralized. All existing supervisor call sites that today invoke notify.notify directly migrate to dispatch_event with a NotifyEvent in F003. NO channel routing by kind, NO debounce/rate-limit, NO retry — those are explicit deferred decisions in decisions.jsonl. The dataclass-and-dispatcher shape is the smallest contract that lets a third sink (Slack/email/push) add without touching emit sites.

(11) Terminal notifications post-adaptation render equivalent title/subtitle/message/group as pre-adaptation for the same event content (regression: synthetic comparison test against fixed before/after values). (12) Module is small (<200 lines incl. shim) — no channel routing, no rate limiting, no retry plumbing.

features.description: Wire the listed emit points in supervisor.py and adjacent modules to call notify_event.dispatch_event with a populated NotifyEvent. Emit points: (a) volley_start (severity=info, kind=volley_start) at the head of dispatch_volley after admission gate clears; (b) gate_paused (severity=action_required, kind=gate_paused, action_link=<INBOX.md path>) when the supervisor pauses on a declared human_gate; (c) breaker_tripped (severity=escalation, kind=breaker_tripped, body includes the breaker-specific kind from BudgetCeilingKind / no_progress / etc., action_link=<INBOX.md path>) when any breaker fires; (d) signoff (severity in {action_required, info} based on signoff verdict, kind=signoff, action_link=<signoff.json path>) at volley closeout; (e) calibration_required (severity=action_required, kind=calibration_required, body includes calibrate-claude command) — already emitted as INBOX event by F006b fix#1 supervisor._emit_budget_kind_specific_event; this slice routes the same event through dispatch_event so Discord sees it. The existing INBOX writer keeps writing unchanged — INBOX is the durable channel; Discord is the live signal. Emit points are surgical: no per-iteration / per-round pings (D059 explicit). The shared invariant at every emit site: INBOX write MUST happen BEFORE dispatch_event call, so the durable record exists even when Discord/terminal sinks fail or are absent. Per-emit-site tests (F004 acceptance items 9-11) prove this ordering by call-order capture against patched INBOX writer + dispatch_event mocks.
